The default slowms threshold is 100 ms and default sampleRate is 1.0. slowms and sampleRate are global (all databases in the process); profiling level and filter are per database when set via db.setProfilingLevel() but process-wide when set on the command line or config file.

Profiler output goes to system.profile, a capped collection per database with a default size of 1 MB (roughly several thousand documents). To resize it, disable profiling, drop it, recreate it with db.createCollection('system.profile', {capped:true, size:N}), then re-enable profiling.

Sampling differs by version: Atlas on 8.x records up to 100 read queries/s per host and no writes; from MongoDB 9.0 $queryStats samples 1% of reads and writes by default (internalQueryStatsSampleRate, internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate, 0.0-1.0). Infrequent shapes may be missing and totals jump after an 8.x to 9.0 upgrade.

- On clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later, Atlas randomly samples 1% of read and write operations by default. Displayed metric values reflect only sampled operations, approximately 1% of total operations. Query shapes that run infrequently may not appear in the results. This method also collects write operations (`insert`, `update`, and `delete`), which appear in Query Shape Insights alongside read operations.
In MongoDB 9.0, the default value changes from `0` to `0.01`, which enables query stats collection for read operations at a default sampling rate of 1%.

Starting in MongoDB 9.0, $queryStats collects stats for a sample of 1% of read and write operations by default. To change the sampling rate, set the internalQueryStatsSampleRate parameter for read operations or the internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate parameter for write operations. Both parameters accept a value between 0.0 and 1.0.

$queryStats stores entries in an in-memory virtual collection limited to 1% of system memory. Each entry is keyed by query shape plus client info, read concern and collection type, so one shape can produce several entries; keyHash identifies the entry and queryShapeHash groups entries by shape.

The slow operation threshold is shared by the profiler and the diagnostic log. With logLevel 0, slow operations are logged at a rate set by slowOpSampleRate; at higher log verbosity all operations are logged regardless of latency.

Slow-query log fields have grown by version: queryFramework (6.2), cpuNanos on Linux (6.3), queues and queryShapeHash (8.0), spill metrics (8.1), originalQueryShapeHash, slow in-progress entries via slowOpInProgressThresholdMs and a deadline field (8.3), and queryKnobs (9.0).

Atlas dynamically adjusts its slow query threshold by default (used by Performance Advisor and Query Profiler); users can opt out to a fixed 100 ms and MongoDB advises against going lower. Free (M0) clusters have the managed threshold disabled and it cannot be enabled; clusters with MongoDB Search do not support it. Toggling needs Project Owner.

Since MongoDB 5.0, changes to profiler level, slowms, sampleRate or filter are written to the log file. Secondaries also log oplog applications slower than the threshold; the profiler does not capture slow oplog entries.
